catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class binds a three-axis linear stage move on motion.axis. cap.motion.joint_position.v1 declares every joint in radians, and this device has linear axes in micrometres whose travel the site supplies; cap.motion.cartesian_pose.v1 is restricted to robot.arm and carries an orientation and inverse-kinematics pose. The extension action takes absolute X, Y and Z targets in micrometres and hands them to the upstream move_um.

notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/amsikking__asi_ms_2000_500_cp --backend fake; all gates G1-G9 pass and no warning was reported; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. gate.digest is the digest the check printed for the passing report; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, decision family-config), but the upstream builds every command from the configured axis tuple at run time (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:157-183 assembles S/AC/WT/PC lines, 311-325 assembles J lines, 353-380 assembles the M line), so a fixed command table cannot reproduce the lines the controller receives. This package is a direct Driver over asi_MS_2000_500_CP:Controller with a native.py hardware factory; a maintainer can correct the card with an override.

Scope and coverage: one controller configured with the three axes ('X','Y','Z'); the upstream also accepts ('X','Y') and ('Z',) (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:39), and those configurations are not served because the resource publishes three named positions and one three-axis move. Reads: X, Y and Z positions in micrometres, motor_moving, PWM intensity in percent, and the PWM state derived from the TTL input/output modes. Writes: pwm_intensity 1 to 99 percent (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:397) and pwm_state off/on/pwm/external (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:407). One extension action, x-cap.amsikking.move_stage.v1, takes absolute X, Y and Z targets in micrometres. Its travel limits are operator_required because the clone takes the travel from the caller's axes_min_mm and axes_max_mm (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:57-64) and the numbers in its test block are example configurations, not stated bounds (asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:443-444). site-limits.example.json is an example overlay, not a statement about any stage.

Safety: the e-stop calls set_pwm_state('off'), the lowest value of the one output this driver sets. The clone exposes no motion-abort command (move_um only starts a move and _finish_moving only waits; asi_MS_2000_500_CP.py:335-380), so a stage move already commanded runs to its target. The package does not claim to stop the stage and is R1; there is no hardware e-stop citation and none is needed at R1.

Fake: an in-memory stand-in for the upstream Controller, not a transcript. The card's mock_strategy preferred a transcript, but the clone ships no tests, simulator or recording (upstream_tests null, hints empty), so there was no session to replay. Every number in fake.py is marked '# placeholder' and none is copied into a Fact, a Limit or a reference. NOT COVERED: velocity, acceleration, settle time and precision settings, joystick enable, status byte, and the raw serial transport.

Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model and reviewed_by is null. Hardware was never attached, the hardware backend was never started, and nothing here ran on a controller or a stage.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-10-30; reviewed_by stays null): accepted; the reviewer changed no file of the package. The DEVIATION FROM THE CARD is accepted: a registry override now makes the card a direct driver. After the registry rebuild refreshed task.json, the reviewer re-ran the gate and wrote its digest above.
